newsitem.title: USA: MGM acquiring big film libary, studio from Metromedia.
newsitem.headline: MGM acquiring big film libary, studio from Metromedia.

text.p: Hollywood studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc. is buying Metromedia International Group Inc.'s entertainment group and huge film library for $573 million, the companies said Monday.
The deal will add movies such as "Dances With Wolves," and "The Silence of the Lambs," to MGM's library, which includes "Midnight Cowboy" and the James Bond series.

The transaction involves Atlanta-based Metromedia's 2,200-title film and television library and the production and distribution activities of its entertainment group, including Orion Pictures Corp., Goldwyn Entertainment Co. and Motion Picture Corp. of America, the companies said.
"This acquisition more than doubles the size of MGM's library, giving it the added distinction of being the largest modern film library in the world," said MGM Chairman Frank Mancuso.
In addition to the library, MGM will acquire 12 completed movies and five direct-to-video features for future release.
Metromedia said the deal will allow it to focus on its telecommunications business.

"This transaction will provide our company with the opportunity to focus our efforts on the expansion of our telecommunications systems in Eastern Europe and the Far East," Metromedia Chairman John Kluge said in a statement. "The development of extensive communications infrastructures is crucial to the economic development of those regions."
The companies said the transaction does not include Metromedia's Landmark Theatre Group, which has a total of 138 screens at 50 locations throughout the United States.

Under the deal, Metromedia's cable television systems will get first crack at MGM movies available in countries where Metromedia operates cable TV networks, including the Metromedia Entertainment Network in Eastern Europe, Metromedia Chief Executive Officer Stuart Subotnick said.
After the acquisition, MGM's combined libraries will consist of more than 3,600 titles, making it the biggest collection of post-1948 movies, the statement said.
The movies being acquired include Oscar winners "Dances With Wolves," "The Silence of the Lambs," "The Best Years of Our Lives," "Wuthering Heights," "Guys and Dolls," and the "RoboCop" series.
MGM already has a 1,600-title collection, including "Midnight Cowboy," "West Side Story", "The Apartment" and the James Bond, Pink Panther and Rocky series.

Along with wireless cable TV systems, Metromedia's telecommunications operations include FM and AM radio broadcasting, paging services and various kinds of telephone service in Eastern Europe, the republics of the former Soviet Union and other emerging markets.
In addition to movies, MGM has a 4,500-title home video library and a television library. Its operating units include MGM Pictures, United Artists Pictures, MGM Music and MGM Interactive.
The deal, which is subject to approval by both companies stockholders, is expected to close this summer.
Metromedia stock rose 37.5 cents to $9.50 in afternoon trading on the American Stock Exchange. MGM is owned by a group of investors led by Kirk Kerkorian.
